fields.fieldText: Customer Account Validation that requires security code. If the customer has ACCESS TO CONTACT EMAIL have the customer get the code and enter it. If not, verify the SECURITY QUESTION and temporarily disable the account access control. Security Code improves the security of your RingCentral account, and reduces the risk of fraudulent activity. Account Validation Disabled - Administrators will still see Account Validation under the Tools section, with the option to enable it for all Users. Once enabled, Account Validation will no longer appear under the Tools section. All Users will be asked to validate their account the next time they try to access it on another device. NOTE: In cases when a User fails to receive the verification codes through SMS on their mobile phone, or through their email address, disable Account Validation temporarily.

fields.name: tileccaf
fields.fieldText:
REASONS FOR SENDING CCAF
  • New account activation from an IN address outside of the U.S.
  • Enabling international calling
  • Activating more than two account on one credit card
  • Activating higher-end auto-purchase amounts
  • Raising the transaction or amount limit per month
  • Activating fax broadcasting
  • Account verification
  • Ownership dispute
REQUEST THE CUSTOMER TO SEND CCAF in order to RESET THE PASSWORD HOW TO SEND CCAF TO RINGCENTRAL:
  • CCAF must be sent via FAX only (800) 520-1568 or (650) 641-2698.
  • Cannot be sent via email
  • Faxes coming in with blocked caller IDs will NOT be processed
Please click the link Credit Card Authorization Form (CCAF) Click this link for RC/UK customer RingCentral UK: CCAF - Credit Card Authorization Form Recommended Dispositions:
  • Create a case and dispose using Internal Work Flow
  • Fraud
  • Verification Required
ESCALATE THE TICKET TO FRAUD Follow the steps
  • Log a ticket and make sure its properly documented Recommended Dispositions:
  • Create a case and dispose using Internal Work Flow
  • Fraud
  • Verification Required
  • Set the Escalate To field on your case ticket to FRAUD INVESTIGATION as seen on the screenshot below
  • Save the ticket
NOTE: Leave the case open and wait for the Fraud Team to verify the account once they received the customer's CCAF within 48 hours.

fields.name: Tile_A
fields.fieldText:
STEPS IN RESETTING ADMINISTRATOR EXTENSION PASSWORD For visual walk-through, Please click the link Article Number : 2397 Please Follow the Steps: Step 1. Log in as an Administrator to your RingCentral Account. Step 2. From the Admin Portal view, switch to My Extension view, and then click Settings. Step 3. Go to User Details and under User Details, click Change Password. Step 4. Enter your Current Password, and then enter and confirm the New Password that you want to assign to the Admin or User. Click Save. Important:
  • for Callers with Admin Access calling in to change Password of Another Extension they will see "Current Admin Password", this refers to their active Admin Password.
  • for Callers with Admin Access calling in to change Password of Their Extension Password they will see "Current Password", this refers to their active Admin Password
The new Password needs to follow the Password Criteria. This criteria makes the User's Password secure and less vulnerable to unauthorized access. The Password must meet the following criteria:
  • One (1) letter
  • One (1) number
  • One (1) special character (!, @, #, $, %, ^, &, * , .) or One (1) uppercase letter
  • At least eight (8) characters with a maximum of 32 characters.
  • No repeating or sequential characters/numbers
Step 5. Please advice them to Log out and Log back in using the new password to ensure that the new password is working. Note: if an Admin or a User completely locks themselves out of the account, Verify Admin or User extension security question and reset the user's password via ADMIN INTERFACE

fields.name: tile1_optionC
fields.fieldText:
FORGOT PASSWORD and RESET PASSWORD At this point you have two options to rectify the log in issue, you could use either the Forgot Password? link or use the reset your password option. FYI: KB articles related to log in issue.
  • Login Issues | RingCentral Online Account
  • Unable to Login | RingCentral Online Account | Forgot Password
  • How to reset password for my online account | RingCentral
Step 1: Utilize the forgot password option at https://service.ringcentral.com Step 2.1 Forgot Password walkthrough
  • Click the Forgot Password? link.
  • Fill out the required fields and click, Reset. Note: make sure the correct Phone Number, Country logo and Extension number is filled up.
  • Check the number used to log in if there’s a “1” at the beginning. Remove the number "1" and try the link again.
  • If you are able to provide the correct information, an email will be sent to the Email Address set on your extension.
  • Access your email account, and open the RingCentral notification email (from: service@ringcentral.com) in your Inbox. Click the link on the email to reset your password. NOTE:If you are unable to find the email in your inbox, look for it in the Spam folder.
  • You will be redirected to the RingCentral page where you can reset your password. Enter your New Password, and then re-enter the same password on the Confirm Password box. Click Save. IMPORTANT: The new Password needs to follow the Password Criteria. This criteria makes the User's Password secure and less vulnerable to unauthorized access.
  • Advice the Caller to Log out and Log back in using the new Password to ensure that the new Password is working.
Step 2.1 reset your password walkthrough
  • Click the reset your password link. NOTE: You will need to specify your Extension Number if there are two (2) or more Administrators on your RingCentral account to avoid confusion from resetting a different User account.
  • An email will be sent to the Email Address set on your extension.
  • Access your email account, and open the RingCentral notification email (from: service@ringcentral.com) in your Inbox. Click the Reset Your Password button, or the link on the email to reset your password.
  • Enter your New Password, and then retype it on the Confirm Password box. Click Save.
NOTE: Your new alphanumeric password must comply with RingCentral's Password Criteria:
  • One (1) letter
  • One (1) number
  • One (1) special character (!, @, #, $, %, ^, &, * , .) or One (1) uppercase letter
  • At least eight (8) characters with a maximum of 32 characters.
  • No repeating or sequential characters/numbers
  • Advice the Caller to Log out and Log back in using the new Password to ensure that the new Password is working.
SCENARIOS: 1. What should I do if my email address is incorrect?
  • Ensure that you enter your correct direct number or extension.
  • If you cannot access your email address, you may call support to change your email address. You will need to answer the security questions for account verification. If you are able to answer the questions, your email will be updated and you may follow the "Reset Password" steps.
2. What if I cannot verify my account?
  • If you are a RingCentral Account Administrator and you are unable to remember the answer to your RingCentral account's security questions, you need to submit a Credit Card Authorization Form (CCAF).
  • If you are a non-Admin User, contact your account administrator to reset your password and to update the email address on your account.

PASSWORD REQUIREMENTS: VERIFICATION is highly required for Admin and User Extension in Resetting or Changing the password. Password and Security Question on your online account, maintain your account's confidentiality and privacy.This guide will walk you through the proper identification and resolution of a Password Reset issue. During troubleshooting, all information you've gathered must be recorded in the case.
  • For ADMIN: verify the Admin Extension security question. As an administrator, you have a full system access. You can add or create new users in the RingCentral system and edit or assign new user extensions. To change the way individual extensions operate, access the Users tab on your RingCentral system settings.
  • For USER: verify the Security question of a specific user extension. As a User, you can manage your own extension such as greetings, call handling, and account credentials like passsword and security question.
SYMPTOM/s:
  • Caller cannot verify the account
  • Caller forgot and cannot retrieve password
  • Caller is locked out due to multiple attempts to access the account
  • Security code required

fields.name: Tile_recommended_steps
fields.fieldText:
RECOMMENDED STEP: • Clear Cache and Cookies Sample verbatim: “Mr/Ms Customer, I recommend we clear your browser’s cache and cookies first to resolve the issue as there is a possibility that previous stored data from the website is causing conflict with the password/recognition of your RingCentral number. I’d like to set your expectation that doing so would also clear out data from other websites that you have visited before (such as saved passwords, browsing history, and online form details). Is that OK with you? You can do this step first in case you encounter similar issues in the future. If customer disagrees: “Sure, that would be no problem. I understand that your other website data is very important as well. I’ll reset your password using our system. One moment please…” If Customer Asked) What are the benefits of clearing the browser cache and cookies?
  • Maximizing Speed and Performance - If you spend a lot of time online or have been visiting websites for a long period, then you may build up a sizeable cache. This may affect the speed and performance of your browser especially when a lot of website data has been accumulated. Clearing the cache frees up some space and may just speed things up again
  • Fixing Browser Errors - There are times when your cache can cause problems when you use your browser. For example, you may find that certain websites are slow to load, will not open, return an error message, hang at a certain point, or otherwise refuse to respond as they should. In many cases, you can fix these kinds of errors by clearing your cache before closing and reopening your browser.
  • Maintaining Security - If you are using a public computer or one that is accessible by other people, then clearing your cache may help protect your privacy. Anyone who uses the computer and the browser after you may be able to see what you have been doing. The cache can also store private data required by some websites, which could give the next user on the computer access to sensitive or personal information. The cache's temporary files may also be a target for adware, malware and virus files.
